identifier: What’s the difference between a payout and a deposit in WooPayments?
statement: After you receive an order via WooPayments, the payment amount (minus our fees) will be added to your account balance. This balance is regularly transferred to your bank account or debit card.

identifier: When will I receive payouts for my WooPayments account balance?
statement: Money that you’ve made with WooPayments must flow through your WooPayments account balance before it’s paid out into your bank account.

identifier: Managing Money with WooPayments: Payouts
statement: Payouts are when some or all of your account balance is sent to your bank account or debit card. Payouts occur automatically by default, but eligible merchants can also request instant payouts.

identifier: WooPayments: Payouts > Payout methods
statement: WooPayments can send payouts to a bank account (all countries) or a debit card (U.S. only).

identifier: Debit cards outside the U.S.
statement: Although Stripe, our payments partner, might allow you to add a debit card even if your account country isn’t the U.S., what they will not do is send payouts to such cards.

identifier: WooPayments: Payouts > Managing payouts

identifier: Why is my account showing a negative balance? > Why doesn’t my payout cover a refund?

identifier: When will I receive payouts for my WooPayments account balance? > Pending funds
statement: When a WooPayments transaction occurs on your site, the money from that transaction takes some time to process before it becomes available to be paid out. During this time, the money is “pending” and is included in the Pending Funds amount.

identifier: When will I receive payouts for my WooPayments account balance? > Pending funds

statement: Because WooPayments is built in partnership with Stripe, they make the final determination on whether or not to temporarily withhold some (or all) of your payouts based on perceived risk factors.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves (NOTE)
statement: Because Stripe, not WooPayments, applies and manages reserves, they are the best ones to contact about it.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves (NOTE)
statement: Our visibility into reserves is very limited. We cannot see why one was applied, nor appeal it on your behalf.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves
statement: Reserves are meant to protect the payments processor (Stripe, in this case) against losses arising from future refunds and disputes.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves
statement: Funds that are withheld as part of a reserve will, in time, be paid out into your bank account as normal once the reserve has ended, minus any refunds or disputes of course.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves > Why is there a reserve on my account?
statement: A reserve may be implemented if Stripe thinks that your business represents a higher than acceptable level of risk.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves > What types of reserves are there?
statement: Stripe uses two types of reserve: fixed and rolling. Either one can also include a balance transfer. The email Stripe sends you will tell you which one applies to your account.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves > Fixed reserve
statement: With a fixed reserve, a specific percentage of funds from each new sale is held until a future release date. On that date, all the funds are returned to your available balance.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves > Rolling reserve
statement: With a rolling reserve, a percentage of funds from each new sale is held back for a set length of time, measured from the date of that sale. Each reserved amount is released on its own schedule, such that money flows in and out of the reserve continuously.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves > Reserve plus balance transfer
statement: Because both a fixed and a rolling reserve only affect new sales, they take time to build up the reserved amount. To cover that gap, Stripe may also move a percentage of your balance into reserve when the reserve is initially applied.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves > Will I lose money? Is this a fine?
statement: No. A reserve is not a fee or a fine, and you do not lose the money. Stripe simply sets a portion of your funds aside for a time instead of paying it out right away.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves > What happens if I get a refund or dispute during a reserve?
statement: If a sale is refunded or disputed while its funds are being held in reserve, those reserved funds are released and used to help cover it.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves > When will the reserve end?
statement: Reserves usually last 30 to 90 days, but Stripe’s email will contain the specific length of your reserve. Keep in mind that the timeline given in the email is not a guarantee that the reserve will end at that time.

identifier: WooPayments: Reserves > When will the reserve end?
statement: A few days before the reserve ends, Stripe will review your account and decide whether to remove the reserve or adjust it.
